previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with alcoholic and HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma s/p TACE, and chronic pelvic fractures was admitted for recurrent abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and low-grade fever. Initial evaluation revealed leukopenia, elevated lactate, and diffuse colon wall thickening on CT concerning for colitis versus portal colopathy. She was treated empirically with ciprofloxacin and metronidazole. During admission, she developed acute anemia requiring transfusion, transient hypoxia with pulmonary edema managed with diuresis, and mild troponin elevation attributed to demand ischemia. Her mental status fluctuated, consistent with hepatic encephalopathy, managed with lactulose. Imaging confirmed a stable pelvic hematoma without active bleeding and no pulmonary embolism. She improved clinically, resumed oral intake, and was discharged to extended care to complete antibiotic therapy via PICC line, with plans for RFA of recurrent HCC and outpatient stress testing.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with HCC. Images reviewed at the ___ tumor
clinic. Local recurrence of HCC in the left lobe of the liver, segment II
lesion. This is small, meets criteria with enhancement and washout and should
be treated with RFA.  // RFA to segment II lesion

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to multiphasic CT from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___, and ___, radiology trainees and
Dr. ___ radiologist. Dr. ___ supervised the
trainee during the key components of the procedure and reviewed and agree with
the trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA:  General anesthesia was administered by the anesthesiology
department.
MEDICATIONS:  For full details please refer to anesthesiology notes.
CONTRAST: 120 ml of Optiray contrast.
Total DLP:  1600 mGy cm

PROCEDURE:  PROCEDURE DETAILS:

Following explanation of the risks, benefits and alternatives to the
procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the patient. The patient
was then brought to the computed tomography suite and placed supine on the
imaging table.  General anesthesia was induced by the anesthesiologist. 
Following scout imaging, the skin was marked and draped in the usual sterile
fashion.

The lesion could not be identified on ultrasound.  Therefore, under CT
fluoroscopy, a cool tip cluster radiofrequency ablation ___ with
2.5cm active probe) was advanced through the intercostal space until the tip
of the probe was just beyond the expected location of the left liver lesion. 
Radiofrequency ablation was performed for two partially overlapping ablations
for a total of 12 minutes each achieving a temperature of 92 and 86 degrees
Celsius respectively.  The max current was 1840 mA. The probe was then
withdrawn under low energy to ablate the access tract.

Contrast enhanced multiphase computed tomography was obtained.  The skin was
then cleaned and a dry sterile dressing was applied. The patient was awakened
from general anesthesia without incident and there were no immediate
post-procedure complications. The patient was transferred to the
post-anesthesia care unit for further monitoring.  The patient has been
scheduled to be admitted under the hepatology service.  The patient's family
has been called to discuss post-procedure status.

FINDINGS: 

Preprocedure noncontrast images demonstrate a cirrhotic liver.  There is a
vague hypodensity seen within the left hepatic lobe (03:17) which
corresponding to the previously embolized site with recurrent HCC.  The lesion
to be treated can be seen as a very mild hypodense area.  The spleen is
nonenlarged.  Bilateral adrenals are unremarkable.  Normal appearance of the
pancreas with no focal lesions.  The main pancreatic duct is not dilated.  A
few renal cysts are noted, with no evidence of hydronephrosis.  There is a
tiny nonobstructing left renal calculus in the mid kidney (03:28).  There is a
recannulized umbilical vein with collaterals in the anterior subcutaneous soft
tissues.  No worrisome osseous findings.  Bilateral segmental atelectasis
noted.  No pleural or pericardial effusion.

Postprocedure noncontrast examination demonstrated hyperdensity in the
ablation site, likely representing coagulation necrosis. There are a few air
locules seen in the adjacent fat, from the procedure.  No perihepatic fluid or
hemorrhage is appreciated.  There mild capsular retraction at the site of
ablation.  Arterial phase images demonstrate peripheral hyperemia around the
lesion site.  There is relative hypoperfusion of the peripheral segment 3 of
the left hepatic lobe.  Portal venous phase demonstrate the borders of the RFA
site, which adequately covers the lesion of concern.

IMPRESSION: 

Uneventful CT-guided RFA of the left hepatic lobe lesion representing
recurrent HCC.
